_purpose: Pre-registration of the frozen model. Committed BEFORE the holdout is read for the first time. Anything in this file that changes after the holdout has been read invalidates the holdout as a test.

code_provenance._note: This is the SHA of the commit containing scripts/train_walkforward.py as it stood when the model was selected -- the code that produced the numbers this freeze is based on. The commit that adds THIS file is a child of it; a config cannot contain the SHA of the commit that carries it. Verify with: git show 8dcf0c6:scripts/train_walkforward.py

estimator._note: penalty, C, solver, fit_intercept and class_weight are sklearn 1.9.0 defaults, written out explicitly so a future default change cannot silently alter the frozen model.

model._selection_rationale: Chosen over lightgbm_inner_es on structural grounds, NOT on a log-loss margin. The two are statistically indistinguishable: mean paired difference 0.0006 log-loss, standard error 0.0052, t = +0.12 on 6 df, LightGBM winning 4 of 7 folds. logistic_rank is deterministic, carries no early-stopping iteration, needs no inner split (so it trains on the year closest to the fold it must predict), has lower fold-to-fold spread (sd 0.0425 vs 0.0460), and wins 2020 -- the regime-break year -- by the largest single-fold margin either model achieves.

features._note: Exact list and order. Every column is derived only from quarters strictly earlier than the row being predicted, enforced by the leakage assertion in scripts/build_features_v1.py.

excluded_target_identities._reason: label_yoy is 1 exactly when eps_diluted > eps_year_ago_adjusted, and eps_growth_yoy is that same difference signed and scaled, so sign(eps_growth_yoy) IS the label (verified 21721/21721 rows). growth_acceleration carries eps_growth_yoy as a term. Both are public on prediction_date -- this is a target identity, not a look-ahead -- and both are asserted against at runtime.

preprocessing._order: rank transform -> impute -> scale -> fit. All steps live inside one sklearn Pipeline, so every parameter is learned on the training window ONLY and merely applied to the evaluation rows.

step_1_rank_transform._reason: These four features reach 4.7e7 with a standard deviation of 4.2e5. Standardizing alone collapses nearly every row to a spike near zero and leaves a linear model unable to use them. QuantileTransformer ignores NaN when fitting and preserves it, so it composes with the imputer that follows.
step_1_rank_transform._fit_scope: training window only, never across folds and never on evaluation rows

step_2_imputation._fit_scope: training window only -- medians are learned there and applied to evaluation rows
step_2_imputation._note: Rows with null features are KEPT, never dropped. Imputation happens after the rank transform so the medians are computed on transformed values.

training_window._definition: Cut on prediction_date, never period_end. prediction_date is filed_date + 1 day -- the first moment the number could have been acted on. period_end is when the quarter ended, which does not bound what was knowable.
training_window.row_selection: prediction_date < 2022-01-01 AND label_yoy is not null

walk_forward_used_for_selection._note: Model selection used an expanding-window walk-forward INSIDE this training window. It is recorded for provenance; the frozen model is refit once on the whole window.

holdout._status: NOT YET READ at the time this file was committed
holdout._metadata_only: Only row counts and the date span were inspected in order to write this file. The holdout label distribution was NOT computed, and the holdout positive rate is unknown at freeze time.

evaluation_protocol.procedure: Fit the pipeline above once on the full training window (2011-2021), then predict every labelled holdout row in a single pass.
evaluation_protocol.no_refitting: The model is NOT refit or updated as it walks through the holdout years.
evaluation_protocol._known_property: This means predictions for 2025 come from a model trained on data ending in 2021, so the model is up to four years stale at the far end of the holdout. This is a deliberate consequence of evaluating once; it is stated here rather than discovered later. Any per-year breakdown of holdout results should be read with it in mind.

success_criterion._status: PRE-REGISTERED before the holdout was read. Both conditions must hold.

constant_baseline._probability_source: the TRAINING window's positive rate (2011-2021). It cannot be the holdout's own rate -- that would use the answer to score the baseline.
constant_baseline.accuracy_on_holdout: equals the holdout's realised positive rate, mechanically, since always-predict-1 is right exactly on the positive rows

success_criterion._the_60_3_percent_trap: The holdout base rate is UNKNOWN and may differ materially from the 60.3% measured on the full panel. Across the seven validation folds the yearly positive rate ranged from 46.5% to 75.1% -- a 28.6-point spread with sd 10.0pp -- so a single number is not a stable property of this data. Accuracy-vs-constant MUST therefore be computed against the holdout's OWN constant baseline, not against 60.3% and not against the training window's 61.0%. Judging the model against 60.3% would reward or punish it for where the holdout base rate happened to land.
success_criterion._why_log_loss_leads: Log-loss does not depend on where the class boundary falls, so it is comparable across periods with different base rates. Accuracy is not. If the two conditions disagree, log-loss is the one that was pre-registered as primary in Phase 2.

walk_forward_reference_numbers._note: What the frozen model achieved in selection. Recorded so holdout degradation is measurable, NOT as a threshold the holdout must clear.

calibration_at_freeze._caveat: The decile table committed in Phase 2 was computed for the log-loss winner, lightgbm_inner_es, before logistic_rank was chosen on structural grounds. logistic_rank's own calibration has NOT been separately tabulated and should be measured on the holdout run.
calibration_at_freeze.guidance: Treat the top 20% as one bucket rather than trusting the ordering between deciles 9 and 10.

environment._note: Recorded because QuantileTransformer, SimpleImputer and LogisticRegression defaults are version-dependent. The estimator params above are written out explicitly to survive a default change, but the transformer internals are not.
